newsitem.title: INDIA: IPO for India's MTNL in 1997/98 ideal, say analysts.
newsitem.headline: IPO for India's MTNL in 1997/98 ideal, say analysts.

text.p: India's state-owned telephone monopoly, Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Ltd (MTNL) should tap overseas markets based on its 1996/97 (April-March) results, analysts said on Wednesday.
MTNL's 1996/97 net profit rose to 8.87 billion rupees ($247.77 million) from 7.27 billion rupees in 1995/96. Sales increased to 39.6 billion rupees from 34.48 billion rupees in the previous year.
Analysts predicted a 25 percent increase in the company's 1997/98 net profit.

"These are MTNL's best years. Demand is strong, and private operators are at least a year away. I expect the company to increase its net by 25 percent in 1997/98," said V. Ramanan, general manager, research at Peregrine Capital India.
He said the results had been better than expected and the company would benefit from great interest among investors in its stock.
The Indian government has debated an overseas stock offering for MTNL several times, but has yet to evolve a concrete plan for this exercise.

Other analysts mirrored that sentiment. "MTNL has always been a prime candidate for government divestment and now is as good a time as any," said Sonal Jhaveri, telecommunications analyst at brokerage HSBC Batlivala and Karani Securities Ltd.
She predicted the company's 1997/98 net profit at 10.1 billion rupees and expected it to add 400,000 telephone lines this year.
MTNL is the fixed line operator in Delhi and Bombay. It operates three million lines, out of a total of 13.1 million lines in India, and has a potential consumer base of 23 million people.

However, analysts expressed concerns over MTNL's falling revenue per line, the government's reluctance to hike domestic tariffs, and the surge in its 1996/97 net profit following a drop in its tax payout.
"The company's revenue fell by two percent per line in 1996/97. The fall is expected to be three percent in 1997/98," said an analyst with a leading Dutch investment bank who asked not to be named.
He said the government would have to revise domestic tariffs upward, and stop subsidising domestic subscribers with revenues from business customers.
"This will ensure that MTNL remains attractive to investors," he added.
